# What must be fixed before a scaling study

This is a prospective design note, not an execution manifest or permission to
extend the current API budget. The completed `core-c2` and `expansion-e1` cohorts
retain their source, scoring rules, failures and separate denominators.

## What the pilot establishes

The four-world formal pilot obtained 56.7/100, with a stratified bootstrap 95%
interval of 44.0–68.3. Model completion was 18/19 infrastructure-healthy episodes;
end-to-end completion was 18/20. The separate three-world expansion obtained
77.2/100 from six episodes with a different request budget and source version.
Their difference is not a scaling result.

Prediction and scientific evidence must be reported separately. The audits found
some unchanged-model predictions before later observations, meaningful local
interventions, and known-family quantitative models. They did not establish a
stable D4 result or full recovery of the original microbial delayed-feedback
loop. Seven structured examples are descriptive; disagreements on two gene-case
dimensions remain unresolved. They cannot estimate a population discovery rate.

## Readiness gates

| Gate | Required record | Pilot implication |
|---|---|---|
| Predictive headroom | Same-observation weak and family-informed references; raw normalized error; failed fits retained | Oscillator and Ising display scores approach saturation. The microbial author reference is accurate but all eight fits were nonconverged. A high diagnostic score does not close either issue. |
| Informative alternatives | Source-data adequacy and a planned separating intervention, with uncertainty | Material source checks found both fixed alternatives adequate in only two of four development cases. This is not a general mechanism-discrimination certificate. |
| Prospective evidence | Immutable model, design and tolerance before target data; independent cutoff custody and preserved failed prefixes | Existing model traces support some ordering claims; new execution modules strengthen software records but are not retroactive certification. |
| Open questions and negative outcomes | Agent-selected question, explicit scope, retained refutation or inconclusive result | Completed execution, nonzero effect and supported scientific finding have different denominators. No mechanism-name answer key is required. |
| Instrumentation controls | Exclude assigned initial values, clamps, instantaneous changes and other known transformations from scientific credit | Known apparatus transformations can predict electrical responses without identifying topology. Per-world semantic review is still needed. |
| Structural generalization | Entire mechanism/structure families withheld from development, with an audited public instrument contract | Random parameters, names and channel permutations alone do not establish resistance to memorization. [Explicit seed exclusions](SEED_EXCLUSIONS.md) prevent reuse of declared development instances, but do not establish structural novelty. |
| Reliable evidence review | Exact trace anchors, provenance, two independent-context judgments and explicit disagreement handling | Six evidence dimensions are more auditable than collapsing observations immediately into one ordinal depth grade. |
| Interface and resource stability | Native isolation, raw return preservation, immutable source and actual aggregate accounting | Analysis replay reproduced 29 TypeErrors in 11 episodes; clearer instructions have not yet been shown to improve GPT performance. |

Readiness is assessed per world and task. Registration, numerical consistency,
mechanism identifiability and model-evaluation readiness are different states.
New experimental worlds should not automatically join a model-ranking aggregate.

The thirteen registered worlds passed a complete Linux regression of 1,883 tests,
with one optional repeated material smoke test skipped. A separate native check
completed the source/snapshot/prediction/target chain for spin echo and population
drift with 10 World attempts and 8 isolated predictor calls. These are engineering
results. The [spin-echo reference](spin_echo/REFERENCE_RESULTS.md) provides a
same-observation, author-informed comparison on six reused instances: 30
pulse/late-echo improvements and six plain-interpolation ties. It does not supply
a GPT result or an unseen-structure test.

The next structural split should withhold a versioned generating construction,
with changed state coupling or dynamical order, from method development. Candidate
constructions include a combined RC/RLC circuit, finite-rate exchange between
magnetic sites, or an added regulatory-memory state in the microbial system.
These are design proposals, not implemented holdouts. Any changed physical
promise must appear in a common, truthful public contract for all comparison
arms. Numerical verification fixtures expose their construction to reviewers;
they must remain distinct from confirmation instances. Classic scientific
principles may already be familiar to a model, even when a generating
construction is withheld from this development workflow.

## A staged future experiment

First choose a small set of worlds with complementary scientific demands and
usable same-data references. Freeze public contracts, task instructions, the
source generator split, inference settings, review rubric and failure handling.
Run a separately labelled interface cohort before selecting the confirmatory
instances. Preserve it even if the interface needs repair; revised source needs
a new cohort rather than replacing its results.

Then vary one resource axis at a time. For inference-budget scaling, hold legal
experiment count/units, analysis allowance, presentation, task and test panels
fixed; vary the maximum model requests. Actual requests, tokens, model latency,
World calls, experimental units and analysis CPU are separate reported costs.
Changing all these limits together is a combined-resource study and must be
named as such. Larger request limits do not guarantee more actual computation.

For example, three worlds × eight fixed instances × request ceilings of
8, 16 and 32 is 72 episodes and at most 1,344 requests, before any preflight or
interface cohort. This is a planning example, not a chosen sample size, power
claim, new ledger, scheduled job or extension of the current 352-attempt cap.
A later budget decision must cover the whole declared cohort and all overhead.
Do not begin a cohort that cannot fit its reserved request budget.

Pair request levels by hidden instance and committed evaluation panel, but run
independent agent sessions and measurement streams. Randomize execution order
across budget levels to reduce service-time confounding. Never tune a model or
change the stopping criterion after seeing another arm's targets. Preserve every
failed or incomplete arm; do not condition the average on successful solutions.

A second experiment may vary experimental access while fixing inference and
analysis limits. Reuse the paired-design machinery only when its source and
panel-binding checks match the frozen experiment. Do not infer this curve from
unequal source-subset sizes or the existing core/expansion cohorts.

## Outcomes to preregister

1. Raw normalized predictive errors and same-data reference differences, with
   world-level results and a fixed macro aggregation. Preserve the historical
   pilot display score for historical comparisons only.
2. Model completion, end-to-end completion and reason-specific failures, with
   distinct denominators and uncertainty. Missing provider usage remains unknown.
3. The six scientific evidence dimensions, each with traceable support and
   unresolved disagreements. A completed negative investigation is not converted
   into a positive discovery count or automatic D4.
4. Cost and efficiency: actual tokens, requests, experiments, analysis compute and
   elapsed time. Report paired effects across budgets with uncertainty; a few
   illustrative successes are not an estimated scaling law.

Future adaptive claim testing must use a prespecified error-control scheme and
separate confirmation streams; repeated peeking at the old three-SE gate is not
such a scheme. The finite single-model mapping protocol covers only its frozen
scalar/readout family under its declared noise assumptions. It does not certify
continuous boundaries, multiple later maps, all response channels, or mechanism
truth. None of these changes should be applied retrospectively to pilot scores.
